title: Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027
official_title: Making continuing appropriations for fiscal year 2027, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Introduced by Rep. Tom Cole (R-OK-4), Chair of the House Appropriations Committee — the committee of referral — and cleared by the House per the latest recorded action. Short-term continuing resolutions with a hard December 4, 2026 expiration date are the standard vehicle Congress uses to avoid a shutdown when full-year appropriations are not enacted by October 1, and they typically clear both chambers under time pressure. The Indian Health Service anomaly amounts, District of Columbia local-spending authority, and survivor payments to the widow and heirs of two deceased members of Congress are the most likely points of pushback in Senate negotiations, though not enough to defeat a shutdown-avoidance measure.
summary: A short-term continuing resolution that keeps the federal government funded at fiscal year 2026 rates and under fiscal year 2026 authorities from October 1, 2026 through December 4, 2026 for all twelve regular appropriations areas, buying Congress time to finish full-year fiscal year 2027 appropriations. It also carries a small set of program-specific anomalies, extends the National Flood Insurance Program authority, and blocks the automatic Member of Congress cost-of-living adjustment during the covered period.
brief: Funds the federal government at fiscal year 2026 levels through December 4, 2026 and extends a handful of expiring authorities including the National Flood Insurance Program.

top_lines.headline: Continuing Resolution Basics
subs: Continues fiscal year 2026 rates and authorities into fiscal year 2027
Covers all 12 regular appropriations areas (Ag, CJS, DoD, E&W, FSGG, DHS, Interior, Labor-HHS-Ed, Legislative, Milcon-VA, State, T-HUD)
Expires on December 4, 2026 or upon enactment of the underlying full-year Act, whichever comes first

top_lines.headline: Defense Restrictions
subs: No new production of items not funded for production in fiscal year 2026
No production-rate increases above those sustained with fiscal year 2026 funds
No new multi-year procurements using advance procurement funding for economic order quantity

top_lines.headline: Program-Specific Anomalies
subs: Additional $75.77M for Indian Health Service — Indian Health Services facility staffing
Additional $8.30M for Indian Health Service — Indian Health Facilities staffing
WIC apportioned up to the rate necessary to maintain participation
SBA business loan program apportioned up to the rate necessary for increased demand
FEMA Disaster Relief Fund apportioned up to the rate necessary for response and recovery

top_lines.headline: Expiring Authority Extensions
subs: National Flood Insurance Program (42 U.S.C. 4016(a) and 4026) extended through December 4, 2026
Livestock Mandatory Reporting Act and Agricultural Marketing Act (7 U.S.C. 1636i, 1635 note) extended through December 4, 2026
TANF and Section 1108(b) of the Social Security Act continued through December 4, 2026

top_lines.headline: Member Compensation & Survivor Payments
subs: $174,000 survivor payment to Alfredia Scott, widow of Rep. David A. Scott (D-GA)
$174,000 payment to the heirs at law of Sen. Lindsey O. Graham (R-SC)
Blocks the Member of Congress automatic cost-of-living adjustment during the covered period

top_lines.headline: District of Columbia Local Funds
subs: DC may expend local funds at the rate set in the Fiscal Year 2027 Local Budget Act of 2026 (Bill 26-0659)
Rate is modified as of the date of enactment of this Act

items.main: Continues fiscal year 2026 appropriations rates and authorities for continuing projects across the 12 regular appropriations acts through December 4, 2026.
items.detail: Section 101 lists the 12 anchor appropriations acts (Ag, CJS, DoD, E&W, FSGG, DHS, Interior, Labor-HHS-Ed, Legislative, Milcon-VA, State, T-HUD) and continues each at fiscal year 2026 rates. Section 106 sets the expiration to whichever of three events occurs first: enactment of the applicable full-year fiscal year 2027 Act, enactment of a full-year Act without a provision for the covered activity, or December 4, 2026. Section 110 requires that only the most limited funding action permitted be used to continue projects.

items.main: Prohibits new starts, production increases, and new multi-year procurements at the Department of Defense during the continuing resolution period.
items.detail: Section 102 bars using continuing-resolution funds for production not funded in fiscal year 2026, production-rate increases above fiscal year 2026 levels, or initiation of projects not previously funded. It also bars new multi-year procurement using advance procurement funding for economic order quantity procurement unless specifically appropriated later.

sections.label: Sections 111-125 — Anomalies and Expiring Authority Extensions

items.main: Provides IHS staffing anomalies of $75.77M for Indian Health Services and $8.30M for Indian Health Facilities to staff and operate facilities opened, renovated, or expanded in fiscal years 2022, 2026, and 2027.
items.detail: Section 123(a) provides an additional rate for operations of $75.77M for the Indian Health Service — Indian Health Services account. Section 123(b) provides an additional $8.30M for the Indian Health Service — Indian Health Facilities account. Both amounts are apportioned up to the rate for operations necessary to staff and operate the covered facilities.

items.main: Extends the National Flood Insurance Program's authority through December 4, 2026 by substituting that date for the September 30, 2026 statutory expiration.
items.detail: Section 121 applies sections 1309(a) and 1319 of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4016(a) and 4026) by substituting the date specified in section 106(3) — December 4, 2026 — for "September 30, 2026". A retroactive-application clause treats the substitution as if it had been in effect on September 30, 2026 if this Act is enacted after that date.

items.main: Continues Small Business Administration general business loan programs, FEMA Disaster Relief Fund response and recovery activities, and Wildland Fire Management wildfire suppression at the rates necessary to meet demand.
items.detail: Section 118 permits the SBA Business Loans Program Account to be apportioned up to the rate for operations necessary to accommodate increased demand for 7(a), 5(g), 503, and 303(b) commitments. Section 122 permits the FEMA Disaster Relief Fund to be apportioned up to the rate necessary to carry out Stafford Act response and recovery activities. Section 125 permits Interior and Forest Service Wildland Fire Management accounts to be apportioned up to the rate necessary for wildfire suppression activities.

sections.label: Sections 126-128 — Mandatory Payments, Survivor Payments, and Member COLA

items.main: Continues TANF and Section 1108(b) of the Social Security Act through December 4, 2026 out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated.
items.detail: Section 126 continues activities authorized by part A of title IV (other than under section 403(c) or 418) and section 1108(b) of the Social Security Act at fiscal year 2026 authority and manner through the date specified in section 106(3), appropriating such sums as may be necessary.

items.main: Appropriates $174,000 each to survivors of two deceased Members of Congress and blocks the Member of Congress automatic cost-of-living adjustment during the continuing resolution period.
items.detail: Section 127 appropriates $174,000 for payment to Alfredia Scott, widow of David A. Scott, late a Representative from Georgia, and $174,000 for payment to the heirs at law of Lindsey O. Graham, late a Senator from South Carolina. Section 128 blocks any adjustment under section 601(a) of the Legislative Reorganization Act of 1946 (2 U.S.C. 4501) relating to cost of living adjustments for Members of Congress during the covered period.

underreported.summary: The bill re-designates each amount previously designated as an emergency or disaster-relief requirement under prior Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act triggers as an emergency requirement under the fiscal year 2022 budget resolution and fiscal year 2027 House budget enforcement, and treats prior disaster-relief designations as continuing.
underreported.why_unreported: Section is captioned to continue "emergency" and "disaster-relief" treatment of amounts referenced elsewhere, but the operative effect is to attach the fiscal year 2027 House budget enforcement designation to those amounts — a scorekeeping choice not visible from the section label.

underreported.summary: The bill permits rescissions and cancellations of discretionary budget authority that were previously scheduled to continue by reducing the rate for operations otherwise provided by section 101 for the current applicable Treasury Appropriations Fund Symbol, capped at the lesser of the prior-Act amount or the balances available as of October 1, 2026.
underreported.why_unreported: Section title reads "Rescissions or cancellations of discretionary budget authority that continue pursuant to section 101" but the mechanical effect is to allow OMB to reduce operating rates for programs receiving current appropriations to absorb previously-scheduled rescissions, with an OMB report to Appropriations Committees due November 20, 2026.

underreported.section: Section 120 — Substitutions in Section 747 of Division E of Public Law 119-75
underreported.summary: The bill substitutes the years 2026 for 2025, 2027 for 2026, and 2028 for 2027 in Section 747 of title VII of division E of the FY2026 Financial Services and General Government Appropriations Act, and updates the underlying statutory reference.
underreported.why_unreported: The section number and mechanical language mask what the substitution does — it advances the year references in the underlying provision by one year, but the plain text of the CR does not restate the underlying provision, so a reader cannot tell what activity the year shift affects.

gaps: The bill covers only 65 days (October 1 through December 4, 2026) and does not address what happens if full-year appropriations are not enacted by December 4, 2026.

The bill anomalies specifically fund the Indian Health Service for staffing new facilities but do not include a similar anomaly for staffing at other federal health facilities opened during the same period.
The bill extends the National Flood Insurance Program authority via Section 121 but leaves the underlying program's transactional ceilings and borrowing authority unchanged.
The bill continues TANF and mandatory payments through December 4, 2026 but does not address the treatment of monthly obligations due for periods after that date if the CR lapses.

The bill blocks the Member of Congress cost-of-living adjustment during the covered period but does not address civilian federal employee pay adjustments that would otherwise take effect in January 2027.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Womack
featured_quotes.text: Mr. Speaker, I rise to support H.R. 9770, the Continuing Appropriations Act of 2027, in hopes that it is not necessary. If we were to complete our work as the Framers had intended and outlined for us, we wouldn't be standing here today. This is an insurance policy. This ensures that, assuming we don't finish our work by the end of September, by the end of this fiscal year, our government will be held harmless. Who could argue an insurance policy that holds a government harmless when we begin a new fiscal year?
